question: A study with a very large sample size (n = 50,000) finds that a new health intervention reduces mean systolic blood pressure by 1 mmHg with p = 0.001. This result is both statistically significant and clinically significant.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Correct — the statement is false. Large sample sizes give enormous statistical power, meaning even tiny, clinically irrelevant differences can achieve p < 0.001. A 1 mmHg blood pressure reduction is statistically detectable in n = 50,000 but is not clinically meaningful. Always consider effect size and clinical context alongside p-values.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: This statement is actually false. A 1 mmHg reduction in blood pressure is below the threshold of clinical significance in most guidelines (typically ≥5 mmHg for meaningful cardiovascular benefit). With n = 50,000, even trivially small differences become statistically significant because the standard error of the mean is very small. Statistical significance (p < 0.05) does NOT imply clinical significance.
